s: something that has been washed ashore
something that has been washed ashore: flood, glut (sudden abundance of something)
an area of shallow water where people or, more often, animals bathe themselves
part of a beer hall or large pub, originally that reserved for the lower classes, now one where people either stand or otherwise sit in large numbers at simple tables
Schwemme.et: From Middle High German swemme, deverbal from swemmen, whence modern schwemmen (“to sweep, to wash ashore”), which see for more. The sense “part of a beer hall” derives via “simple tavern” (16th c.) from the formerly current expression die Zunge in die Schwemm…

schwemmen.et: From Middle High German swemmen, from Old High German *swemmen, from Proto-Germanic *swammijaną. Equivalent to a causative of schwimmen, thus originally “to make swim or float”. Cognate with Old English beswemman.

t: Der Regen schwemmte den Erboden weg.
